date_note: Date of the Mainichi Shimbun's announcement as reported by Cybersecurity.com (Japan); the unauthorized access to KARTE was in the early hours of 13 Nov.
title: Mainichi Shimbun says surnames of about 140,000 digital members leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
summary: The Mainichi Shimbun announced on 19 November that part of its Mainichi Shimbun Digital member data leaked through unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE, used by its news app, according to Cybersecurity.com (Japan). Confirmed leaked: surnames of about 140,000 members, about 70,000 ages, about 18,000 plan names, about 2,700 points-club IDs and about 80 email addresses. The company says no misuse has been confirmed so far.
plain: A big Japanese newspaper says members' surnames and some ages, plan names and emails leaked when a supplier's system was hacked. No misuse is known yet.
exec: A supplier breach exposed surnames of about 140,000 digital members of a national newspaper, with no misuse confirmed so far.
action: The Mainichi Shimbun urges members not to open links or attachments in suspicious emails, as reported by Cybersecurity.com (Japan).

evidence.quote: 漏えいが確認されたのは、会員約14万人分の姓のほか、年齢約7万件、契約プラン名約1万8,000件、まいにちポイントくらぶのID約2,700件、メールアドレス約80件である。

validation.note: Only Cybersecurity.com (Japan) read; it relays the Mainichi Shimbun's announcement. Mainichi's own sites block automated readers, so its notice was not read; Impress Watch, innovatopia and SBBIT pages checked do not mention Mainichi.
